subject: Peninsula pilot — cost acceptance & MAP QA
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morris <kate.morris@peninsulahealth.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@peninsulahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Peninsula pilot — cost acceptance & MAP QA

Hi Kate —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our agreement, I’m attaching an initial MAP worksheet that ties together the pilot evaluation plan, timelines, and the unit-econ checks Peninsula asked us to gate on. The quick ask from my side: please confirm whether Procurement wants the MAP as a single shared workbook (we uploaded a folder link below) or as separate deliverables (SOW + econ workbook + evaluation checklist).

High-level we propose the following acceptance gates for the pilot before a full roll-out:
- Cost threshold: unit token cost (after caching/batching assumptions) must be <= $0.0006/token effective for the pilot workload (we show tokens/$ equivalence in the attached).
- Latency SLO: 95th perc tail for production-like traffic < 400ms for 512-token requests (cold-starts excluded).
- Quality: no >5% regression on your test prompts vs baseline model.

Key econ notes in the attachment: tokens per $ at $0.0006/token ~ 1,667 tokens/$. We’ve included two scenarios:
- Conservative: no prefix caching, minimal batching (avg batch size 1.8) — used for procurement worst-case.
- Typical: prefix caching enabled (estimated 22% token reduction), workload-aware batching (avg batch size 4) — reduces effective cost by ~28% vs conservative.

Evaluation plan we recommend: 10k representative calls (mirroring your traffic profile) across three pods and one workload variant. We’ll run the eval, store traces, and provide a short report with token counts, cache hit rates, and per-route unit-econ.

Attachment: peninsula_map_v1.xlsx (MAP worksheet)

Next steps: confirm deliverable format and whether Alex wants to loop Legal early for a narrow pilot SOW. I’ll follow up with an internal note to align our econ assumptions.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Diego — the workbook looks useful. A few clarifying Qs from Procurement:

1) When you quote $0.0006/token, is that the hosted API list price or the pilot effective price after the batching/caching gains you show? We need a clear "procurement" number (what will be on the invoice if we run the pilot).
2) Can you call out whether the caching assumptions require any client-side instrumentation or controlled session affinity? We have strict session routing rules.
3) For the evaluation run — will Redwood provide the scripts and synthetic traffic generator, or do we need to provision a dataset?

If you can produce a one-page summary for Legal/Finance with the invoiceable pilot rate + acceptance criteria, that will speed an internal review.

—Kate

- Procurement number: what do we commit to for the pilot invoice? I suggest we present two invoiceable lines: (a) Pilot compute @ hosted pilot rate $0.00072/token (no discount) and (b) Pilot effective rate "guarantee" assuming caching/batching results (we can offer an operational credit if cache/hit and batching assumptions are met) — illustrated as effective $0.00058/token. Is that acceptable?

Reply-all so I can fold into the one-pager.

Diego

Subject: Re: Peninsula pilot — cost acceptance & MAP QA

Kate — quick follow-up and summary for Legal/Finance attached. TL;DR answers:

1) Invoiceable pilot rate: we will invoice at the standard pilot compute rate of $0.00072/token. To address Procurement’s concern, Redwood will offer an operational adjustment (credit) tied to measured caching and batching during the pilot. If measured effective cost (post cache & batching) <= $0.0006/token for the pilot workload, Redwood will apply a credit equal to the difference for pilot consumption only. This keeps invoice simple but meets your gate.

2) Caching ops: prefix caching is server-side within the Redwood runtime and does not require client-side SDK changes. The only operational ask is a stable session identifier passed in the call metadata to maximize reuse for session-scoped prompts. No changes to your existing routing are required, but we recommend light affinity for high reuse cases.

3) Eval artifacts: Redwood will deliver the traffic generator, runbook, and a Jupyter notebook with the analysis scripts. We will also provide a short SOC2-compliant trace export for your auditors (PII redaction options available).

Attached: peninsula_map_v1.xlsx, redwood_token_econ_breakdown.pdf

Acceptance criteria (finalized):
- Invoiceable: $0.00072/token charged during pilot; operational credit applied post-pilot if effective cost <= $0.0006/token.
- Technical: prefix caching enabled, session-id header recommended, average observed batch size >= 3.5, cache hit rate >= 18% on representative workload.
- Eval: 10k real-ish calls + 3 synthetic runs across 3 pods; report due within 5 business days of run completion.

Next steps: Kate — if that approach works, I’ll ask Legal to draft a 1-paragraph pilot billing addendum for the SOW and share it with Procurement. Alex — tagging you for awareness on the acceptance credit.

Thanks all —
Diego
(attachment: redwood_token_econ_breakdown.pdf, peninsula_map_v1.xlsx)
